The majority read ﴿ʿabdahu﴾ ("His servant"), and this is the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ). Abu Ja'far, Mujahid, Ibn Wathhab, Talhah, al-A'mash, Hamzah and al-Kisa'i read ﴿ʿibadahu﴾ ("His servants") in the plural, meaning: the prophets and the obedient believers.

﴿And they frighten you with those other than Him﴾: namely the idols. When [the Prophet] sent Khalid to break al-'Uzza, its custodian said to him: "I fear for you from it, for it has a power before which nothing stands." Khalid took the axe, struck its face with it and shattered it, then departed. In His saying ﴿they frighten you﴾ there is mockery of them, because they frightened him with what cannot benefit or harm. A parallel to this frightening is the saying of the people of Hud to him: ﴿We only say that some of our gods have struck you with evil﴾ [Hud: 54]. It was also read: ﴿bi-kafin ʿabdahu﴾ ("with a sufficient one of His servant") in the genitive construction, and ﴿yukafi ʿibadahu﴾ as the present tense of kafa, with ﴿ʿibadahu﴾ in the accusative. It is possible that it is a mufa'alah from sufficiency (al-kifayah), like your saying "yujazi" for "yajzi," and it is more emphatic than kafa, for being built upon the form of intensification; and this is the apparent reading because of the frequent recurrence of this meaning in the Qur'an, as in His saying: ﴿So Allah will suffice you against them﴾ [al-Baqarah: 137]. It is also possible that it is hamzated from al-mukafa'ah, which is recompense, meaning: He will recompense them their reward.

Since the Exalted is sufficient for His servant, frightening with other than Him is vain and false.

Since the verse contains both the guided and the misguided, He informed that all of that is done by Him. Then He said: ﴿Is not Allah Mighty﴾, meaning: victorious, unassailable, ﴿Lord of retribution﴾. In this there is a threat to the Quraysh and a promise to the believers.

Since they acknowledged the Creator, who is Allah, He informed them that He, the Exalted, is the One who disposes of His Prophet as He wills. For those idols which they claim to be gods besides Him cannot remove harm nor withhold mercy, meaning: health and abundance in provision and the like.

"Have you considered?" here is used in its original form; it took its first object, which is ﴿what you call upon﴾. The second object came as an interrogative clause, and in it is the pronoun referring back to "what," namely the word ﴿hunna﴾, and it was made feminine to belittle them, render them powerless and diminish them. Among them were those named with female names, such as al-'Uzza, Manat and al-Lat.

He attributed the will of Allah regarding harm to Himself and mercy to Himself, because they frightened him with their harm, so He secured from them the admission that the Creator of the world is Allah.

Then He asked them about their idols: do they remove evil (p-430) and bring about good? The majority read ﴿kashifatu wa-mumsikatu﴾ with the genitive construction; Shaybah, al-A'raj, Amr ibn 'Ubayd and 'Isa read it with variation from him; Abu 'Amr and Abu Bakr read them with tanwin and the accusative for what follows them.

Since it was established that He, the Exalted, is sufficient for him, and that their idols neither harm nor benefit, He commanded him to know that He, the Exalted, is his sufficiency, meaning: his sufficient one. The answer to this question is omitted, and the estimate is: "Surely they will say: you have no power over any of that." Muqatil said: He asked them and they were silent.

﴿Say: O my people, act﴾: the discussion of its parallel has already preceded.

﴿Who then is more unjust than one who lies about Allah and denies the truth when it comes to him? Is there not in Hell an abode for the disbelievers?﴾ ﴿And the one who brings the truth and confirms it: those are the righteous.﴾ ﴿For them is whatever they wish with their Lord. That is the reward of the good-doers.﴾ ﴿That Allah may expiate from them the worst of what they did and reward them with the best of what they used to do.﴾ ﴿Is Allah not sufficient for His servant? Yet they frighten you with those other than Him. And whomever Allah leaves astray, for him there is no guide.﴾ ﴿And whomever Allah guides, for him there is no misleader. Is Allah not Mighty, Lord of Retribution?﴾ ﴿And if you asked them, "Who created the heavens and the earth?" they would surely say, "Allah." Say, "Have you considered what you invoke besides Allah? If Allah intends harm for me, can they remove His harm? Or if He intends mercy for me, can they withhold His mercy?" Say, "Allah is sufficient for me; upon Him rely those who rely."﴾ ﴿Say, "O my people, act according to your position; indeed I am acting. So you will soon know.﴾ ﴿Upon whom will come a punishment that disgraces him, and upon whom will descend a lasting punishment."﴾ ﴿Indeed, We have sent down to you the Book for mankind with the truth. So whoever is guided, it is for his own self; and whoever goes astray, he strays only to its detriment. And you are not a guardian over them.﴾ [Az-Zumar: 41] ﴿Allah takes the souls at the time of their death, and those that have not died during their sleep. Then He keeps those for which He has decreed death and releases the others until a specified term. Indeed, in that are signs for a people who reflect.﴾ [Az-Zumar: 42] ﴿Or have they taken intercessors besides Allah? Say, "Even though they possess nothing and do not understand?"﴾ [Az-Zumar: 43] (p-426) ﴿Say, "To Allah belongs all intercession. To Him belongs the dominion of the heavens and the earth. Then to Him you will be returned."﴾ [Az-Zumar: 44] ﴿And when Allah alone is mentioned, the hearts of those who do not believe in the Hereafter shrink; but when those other than Him are mentioned, behold, they rejoice.﴾ [Az-Zumar: 45] ﴿Say, "O Allah, Creator of the heavens and the earth, Knower of the unseen and the witnessed, You will judge between Your servants concerning that over which they used to differ."﴾ [Az-Zumar: 46] ﴿And if those who wronged had all that is in the earth and the like of it with it, they would surely ransom themselves with it from the evil of the punishment on the Day of Resurrection. And there will appear to them from Allah what they had not expected.﴾ [Az-Zumar: 47] ﴿And there will appear to them the evils of what they earned, and they will be surrounded by that which they used to mock.﴾ [Az-Zumar: 48] ﴿So when harm touches man, he calls upon Us; then when We bestow upon him a favor from Us, he says, "I was given it only because of knowledge." Rather, it is a trial, but most of them do not know.﴾ [Az-Zumar: 49] ﴿Those before them had said it, but what they used to earn did not avail them.﴾ [Az-Zumar: 50] ﴿So the evils of what they earned struck them. And those who wronged among these will be struck by the evils of what they earned, and they cannot escape.﴾ [Az-Zumar: 51] ﴿Do they not know that Allah extends provision to whom He wills and restricts it? Indeed, in that are signs for a people who believe.﴾ [Az-Zumar: 52] ﴿Say, "O My servants who have transgressed against themselves, do not despair of the mercy of Allah. Indeed, Allah forgives all sins. Indeed, He is the Forgiving, the Merciful."﴾ [Az-Zumar: 53] ﴿And turn in repentance to your Lord and submit to Him before the punishment comes upon you, after which you will not be helped.﴾ [Az-Zumar: 54] ﴿And follow the best of what was revealed to you from your Lord before the punishment comes upon you suddenly while you do not perceive.﴾ [Az-Zumar: 55] ﴿Lest a soul should say, "Oh, my regret over what I neglected in regard to Allah, and indeed I was among the mockers."﴾ [Az-Zumar: 56] ﴿Or lest it say, "If only Allah had guided me, I would have been among the righteous."﴾ [Az-Zumar: 57] ﴿Or lest it say when it sees the punishment, "If only I had another return, I would be among the good-doers."﴾ [Az-Zumar: 58] ﴿[It will be said], "Yes, indeed My verses came to you, but you denied them, grew arrogant, and were among the disbelievers."﴾ [Az-Zumar: 59] ﴿And on the Day of Resurrection you will see those who lied about Allah with their faces blackened. Is there not in Hell an abode for the arrogant?﴾ [Az-Zumar: 60] ﴿And Allah will save those who were righteous by their achievement; no harm will touch them, nor will they grieve.﴾ [Az-Zumar: 61] ﴿Allah is the Creator of all things, and He is the Guardian over all things.﴾ [Az-Zumar: 62] ﴿To Him belong the keys of the heavens and the earth. And those who disbelieved in the signs of Allah, those are the losers.﴾ [Az-Zumar: 63] ﴿Say, "Do you command me to worship other than Allah, O ignorant ones?"﴾ [Az-Zumar: 64] ﴿And it has been revealed to you and to those before you: "If you associate partners with Allah, your deeds will surely be lost, and you will surely be among the losers."﴾ [Az-Zumar: 65] ﴿Rather, worship Allah alone and be among the grateful.﴾ [Az-Zumar: 66] ﴿They did not measure Allah with His true measure. And the earth entirely in His grip on the Day of Resurrection, and the heavens folded in His right hand. Glorified is He and exalted above what they associate with Him.﴾ [Az-Zumar: 67] ﴿And the Trumpet will be blown, and whoever is in the heavens and whoever is on the earth will fall unconscious, except whom Allah wills. Then it will be blown again, and immediately they will be standing, looking on.﴾ [Az-Zumar: 68] ﴿And the earth will shine with the light of its Lord, the Record will be placed, the prophets and the witnesses will be brought, and judgment will be given between them with truth, and they will not be wronged.﴾ [Az-Zumar: 69] ﴿And every soul will be paid in full for what it did, and He is most knowing of what they do.﴾ [Az-Zumar: 70] ﴿And those who disbelieved will be driven to Hell in groups, until when they reach it, its gates will be opened, and its keepers will say to them, "Did there not come to you messengers from among you reciting to you the verses of your Lord and warning you of the meeting of this your Day?" They will say, "Yes, but the word of punishment has come due upon the disbelievers."﴾ [Az-Zumar: 71] ﴿It will be said, "Enter the gates of Hell, to abide therein. How wretched is the abode of the arrogant."﴾ [Az-Zumar: 72] ﴿And those who feared their Lord will be driven to Paradise in groups, until when they reach it, and its gates are opened, its keepers will say to them, "Peace be upon you; you are good, so enter it to abide therein."﴾ [Az-Zumar: 73] ﴿And they will say, "Praise be to Allah, who has fulfilled His promise to us and has caused us to inherit the earth, to dwell in Paradise wherever we will. How excellent is the reward of the workers."﴾ [Az-Zumar: 74] ﴿And you will see the angels surrounding the Throne, glorifying their Lord with His praise. And judgment will be given between them with truth, and it will be said, "Praise be to Allah, Lord of the worlds."﴾ [Az-Zumar: 75].

Ishma'azza (اشمأز): Abu Zayd said: "za'ira" (زعر). Others said: "taqabbaḍa karāhatan wa-nufūran" (it contracted from aversion and repulsion). The poet said:

*"When the trustworthy ones bite at it, it shrinks, and it turns away from him, rough and strong."*

Al-maqalid (المقاليد): the keys (al-mafatih). It was said: it has no singular from its own form, as stated by al-Tabrizi. It was also said: its singular is miqlid, and it was said: miqlad. It is said: iqlid and aqalid. The word originally is Persian.

Al-zumar (الزمر): the plural of zumra. Abu 'Ubayda and al-Akhfash said: separate groups, one following another. He said:

*"Until the groups gathered, one after another."*

It is said: tazammara (to form groups).

Al-hufuf (الحفوف): surrounding something (al-ihdaq bi-l-shay'). The poet said:

*"Surrounded by a narrow side, and followed by it, like a glass bottle not treated with kohl against sore eyes."*

This word is derived from al-hafaf, which is the side. From it is the saying of the poet:

*"For him are glances from the side of his throne, when he returns them there is punishment and bounty."*

﴿So who is more unjust than one who lies about Allah...﴾ up to ﴿...an abode for the disbelievers﴾ [quoted above]. ﴿...And the one who brings the truth and confirms it...﴾ [quoted above].

﴿Who then is more unjust than one who lies about Allah﴾: This is an explanation and clarification of those who have the dispute, and this indicates that the earlier dispute (ikhtisam) is between the believers and the disbelievers. The meaning: I find among the deniers no one more unjust than one who fabricates against Allah, attributing to Him a son, a consort, and a partner, and makes lawful and unlawful without the command of Allah.

﴿And denies the truth﴾: which is what the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) brought. ﴿When it comes to him﴾: i.e., at the time of its coming. He confronts it with denial without thought, reflection, or consideration; rather, at the very time of its coming he denies it.

Then He threatens them with a threat containing belittlement of them, in the manner of a rebuke. The word "for the disbelievers" is where the apparent noun is placed in the position of the pronoun, i.e., "an abode for them." In this there is an alert to the cause of their lying and denial, which is disbelief (kufr).

﴿And the one who brings the truth﴾ is parallel to His saying: "Who then is more unjust."

﴿And confirms it﴾ is opposite to His saying: ﴿and denies the truth﴾. ("Alladhi") is a generic term, as if He said: "And the group who brought the truth." This is indicated by ﴿those are the righteous﴾, so He used the plural. Just as the intended meaning of "who then is more unjust" is a plural, which is why He said "an abode for the disbelievers."

In the recitation of Abdullah (Ibn Mas'ud): "And those who brought the truth and confirmed it" (wa-lladhi ja'u bi-l-sidq wa-saddaqu bihi). It was said: He intended "alladhina" (those who), and the nun was dropped. This is not correct, since if "alladhina" were intended with the form "alladhi" and the nun dropped, the pronoun would have been plural, as in His saying:

*"And indeed, those whose blood was shed at Falh..."*

Do you not see that when the nun is dropped in the dual, the pronoun becomes dual? As in His saying:

*"Sons of Kulayb, indeed my two uncles, who killed the kings and freed the shackles."*

It was said: "The one who brought the truth and confirmed it" is the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ).

It was said: "The one who brought the truth" is Jibril (Gabriel), and "the one who confirmed it" is Muhammad (ﷺ).

Ali, Abu al-'Aliya, al-Kalbi, and a group said: "The one who brought the truth" is the Messenger, and "the one who confirmed it" is Abu Bakr.

Abu al-Aswad, Mujahid, and a group said: "The one who confirmed it" is Ali ibn Abi Talib.

Al-Zamakhshari said: "And the one who brought the truth and confirmed it" is the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), who brought the truth and believed in it, and by it he intended himself and those who followed him, just as by Musa he intended himself and his people in His saying: ﴿And indeed We gave Musa the Book that they might be guided﴾ [Al-Mu'minun: 49]. For this reason He said: ﴿those are the righteous﴾, except that this is in the attribute and that is in the noun.

It is also permissible that the intended meaning is: the group and the company who brought the truth and confirmed it, namely the Messenger who brought the truth, and his companions who confirmed it. End of quote.

His statement "by it he intended himself and those who followed him, just as by Musa he intended himself and his people" uses the detached pronoun in a place where it should be attached. The correct form would be: "and intended him by it and those who followed him, just as he intended him with Musa and his people," meaning: "perhaps his people would be guided," since Musa (peace be upon him) is himself guided. Thus what is hoped for is the guidance of his people, not his own guidance, since only what is absent, not what is present, is hoped for.

His statement "and it is permissible etc." contains a distribution of the relative clause (tawzi' al-silah), where "the group" is the relative antecedent; it is like his saying: "The group came, which was honored and honored others." The more apparent view is that there is no distribution; rather, what is conjoined to the relative clause is a relative clause for the one who has the first relative clause.

Al-Jumhur (the majority) recited "wa-saddaqa" with shaddah (emphatic), while Abu Salih, 'Ikrima ibn Sulayman, and Muhammad ibn Juhaza recited it without shaddah. Abu Salih said: "and acted upon it."

It was said: "he deserved by it the name of truthfulness." Ibn 'Atiyya said: "According to this, all the verbs are ascribed to Muhammad (ﷺ), and his community is implicitly included in the speech, and this is what makes ﴿those are the righteous﴾ fitting." End of quote.

Al-Zamakhshari said: that is, "he confirmed the people by it and did not lie to them about it," meaning: he conveyed it to them as it was revealed to him, without distortion. It was also said: its meaning is "he became truthful by it," i.e., by means of it, because the Qur'an is a miracle, and a miracle is a confirmation from the Wise One who does not do what is ugly toward the one through whose hands it is performed, and it is not permissible that one should be confirmed except a truthful one, so he becomes truthful by the miracle.

It has been recited: ﴿wa-saddaqa bihi﴾ (with the verb in the passive form, shaddah). End of quote. He means: in the passive voice with shaddah. The author of al-Lawami' said: "He came with truth from Allah, and he confirmed it by His word," i.e., in His word or in His coming, so the two qualities of truth were combined for him: his truthfulness from Allah, and his truthfulness in himself, and this is an intensification in praise. End of quote.

(p-427)

Commentary of Abu Hayyan (al-Bahr al-Muhit) on surah 39, verse 32–40 (part 2 of 2):

﴿They shall have whatever they wish﴾: general in respect of everything their souls desire and their wills are directed toward. And ﴿so that﴾ (li-yukaffira): it is connected either to "the good-doers," meaning: those who did good, so that [Allah] may expiate; or to an omitted element, meaning: He facilitated that for them so that He may expiate, because expiation only occurs after facilitation toward good. And ﴿the worst of what they did﴾ refers to the disbelief of the people of ignorance (jahiliyyah) and the sins of the people of Islam. (p-429) Expiation indicates the removal of punishment from them in the most complete manner, and recompense with "the best" indicates the attainment of reward in the most complete manner. It has been said: that occurs when they affirm the prophets in what they brought. Muqatil said: He recompenses them with the good deeds among their actions and does not recompense them with the bad ones. This is the view of the Murji'ah, who say: no sin harms alongside faith. They argued with this verse. The apparent noun stands in place of the pronoun in "the good-doers," meaning: that is their recompense, so by the apparent noun He draws attention to the cause that necessitates the attainment of reward. The apparent reading is that "worst" (asw'a) is an elative (af'al al-tafdil), and with it the majority (al-Jumhur) read: "and when He expiates the worst of their deeds," so expiating what is lesser than it is more fitting. It has been said: af'al is not for comparison, and it is like your saying: "al-Ashajj is the most just of the Banu Marwan," meaning: just. Likewise here, meaning: "the evil of those who did [evil]."
This interpretation is supported by the reading of Ibn Miqsam and Hamid ibn Yahya, from Ibn Kathir: "asw'a" here; and in (Ha Mim al-Sajdah) with an alif between the waw and the hamzah, the plural of "su'" (evil), in which there is no elative. The apparent reading is that ﴿the best﴾ is an elative. It has been said: ﴿so that He may look at the best of their acts, and the remainder is recompensed by analogy to it, even if it falls short of that through shortcoming.﴾ It has been said: ﴿the best reward of their deeds.﴾ It has been said: ﴿the best of their deed, which is Paradise,﴾ and this is repelled by ﴿the best of what﴾.

Al-Zamakhshari said: As for the elative, it indicates that the thing which befalls them of minor sins and slips that are expiated is, in their view, the worst, because of their great regard for disobedience, while the good they do is, with Allah, the best, because of the sincerity of their intention in it. Therefore He mentioned their evil with "the worst" and their good with "the best." End.

This is according to the view of the Mu'tazilah, and it would make "asw'a" an elative according to their belief and "ahsan" an elative according to what is with Allah; and that is a distribution (tawzi') in the elative, which is contrary to the apparent meaning.

And those who wronged among these will be struck by the evils of what they earned, and they cannot escape.﴾ [Az-Zumar: 51] ﴿Do they not know that Allah extends provision to whom He wills and restricts it? Indeed, in that are signs for a people who believe.﴾ [Az-Zumar: 52] ﴿Say, "O My servants who have transgressed against themselves, do not despair of the mercy of Allah. Indeed, Allah forgives all sins. Indeed, He is the Forgiving, the Merciful."﴾ [Az-Zumar: 53] ﴿And turn in repentance to your Lord and submit to Him before the punishment comes upon you, after which you will not be helped.﴾ [Az-Zumar: 54] ﴿And follow the best of what was revealed to you from your Lord before the punishment comes upon you suddenly while you do not perceive.﴾ [Az-Zumar: 55] ﴿Lest a soul should say, "Oh, my regret over what I neglected in regard to Allah, and indeed I was among the mockers."﴾ [Az-Zumar: 56] ﴿Or lest it say, "If only Allah had guided me, I would have been among the righteous."﴾ [Az-Zumar: 57] ﴿Or lest it say when it sees the punishment, "If only I had another return, I would be among the good-doers."﴾ [Az-Zumar: 58] ﴿[It will be said], "Yes, indeed My verses came to you, but you denied them, grew arrogant, and were among the disbelievers."﴾ [Az-Zumar: 59] ﴿And on the Day of Resurrection you will see those who lied about Allah with their faces blackened. Is there not in Hell an abode for the arrogant?﴾ [Az-Zumar: 60] ﴿And Allah will save those who were righteous by their achievement; no harm will touch them, nor will they grieve.﴾ [Az-Zumar: 61] ﴿Allah is the Creator of all things, and He is the Guardian over all things.﴾ [Az-Zumar: 62] ﴿To Him belong the keys of the heavens and the earth. And those who disbelieved in the signs of Allah, those are the losers.﴾ [Az-Zumar: 63] ﴿Say, "Do you command me to worship other than Allah, O ignorant ones?"﴾ [Az-Zumar: 64] ﴿And it has been revealed to you and to those before you: "If you associate partners with Allah, your deeds will surely be lost, and you will surely be among the losers."﴾ [Az-Zumar: 65] ﴿Rather, worship Allah alone and be among the grateful.﴾ [Az-Zumar: 66] ﴿They did not measure Allah with His true measure. And the earth entirely in His grip on the Day of Resurrection, and the heavens folded in His right hand. Glorified is He and exalted above what they associate with Him.﴾ [Az-Zumar: 67] ﴿And the Trumpet will be blown, and whoever is in the heavens and whoever is on the earth will fall unconscious, except whom Allah wills. Then it will be blown again, and immediately they will be standing, looking on.﴾ [Az-Zumar: 68] ﴿And the earth will shine with the light of its Lord, the Record will be placed, the prophets and the witnesses will be brought, and judgment will be given between them with truth, and they will not be wronged.﴾ [Az-Zumar: 69] ﴿And every soul will be paid in full for what it did, and He is most knowing of what they do.﴾ [Az-Zumar: 70] ﴿And those who disbelieved will be driven to Hell in groups, until when they reach it, its gates will be opened, and its keepers will say to them, "Did there not come to you messengers from among you reciting to you the verses of your Lord and warning you of the meeting of this your Day?" They will say, "Yes, but the word of punishment has come due upon the disbelievers."﴾ [Az-Zumar: 71] ﴿It will be said, "Enter the gates of Hell, to abide therein. How wretched is the abode of the arrogant."﴾ [Az-Zumar: 72] ﴿And those who feared their Lord will be driven to Paradise in groups, until when they reach it, and its gates are opened, its keepers will say to them, "Peace be upon you; you are good, so enter it to abide therein."﴾ [Az-Zumar: 73] ﴿And they will say, "Praise be to Allah, who has fulfilled His promise to us and has caused us to inherit the earth, to dwell in Paradise wherever we will. How excellent is the reward of the workers."﴾ [Az-Zumar: 74] ﴿And you will see the angels surrounding the Throne, glorifying their Lord with His praise. And judgment will be given between them with truth, and it will be said, "Praise be to Allah, Lord of the worlds."﴾ [Az-Zumar: 75].

Ishma'azza (اشمأز): Abu Zayd said: "za'ira" (زعر). Others said: "taqabbaḍa karāhatan wa-nufūran" (it contracted from aversion and repulsion). The poet said:

*"When the trustworthy ones bite at it, it shrinks, and it turns away from him, rough and strong."*

Al-maqalid (المقاليد): the keys (al-mafatih). It was said: it has no singular from its own form, as stated by al-Tabrizi. It was also said: its singular is miqlid, and it was said: miqlad. It is said: iqlid and aqalid. The word originally is Persian.

Al-zumar (الزمر): the plural of zumra. Abu 'Ubayda and al-Akhfash said: separate groups, one following another. He said:

*"Until the groups gathered, one after another."*

It is said: tazammara (to form groups).

Al-hufuf (الحفوف): surrounding something (al-ihdaq bi-l-shay'). The poet said:

*"Surrounded by a narrow side, and followed by it, like a glass bottle not treated with kohl against sore eyes."*

This word is derived from al-hafaf, which is the side. From it is the saying of the poet:

*"For him are glances from the side of his throne, when he returns them there is punishment and bounty."*

﴿So who is more unjust than one who lies about Allah...﴾ up to ﴿...an abode for the disbelievers﴾ [quoted above]. ﴿...And the one who brings the truth and confirms it...﴾ [quoted above].

﴿Who then is more unjust than one who lies about Allah﴾: This is an explanation and clarification of those who have the dispute, and this indicates that the earlier dispute (ikhtisam) is between the believers and the disbelievers. The meaning: I find among the deniers no one more unjust than one who fabricates against Allah, attributing to Him a son, a consort, and a partner, and makes lawful and unlawful without the command of Allah.

﴿And denies the truth﴾: which is what the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) brought. ﴿When it comes to him﴾: i.e., at the time of its coming. He confronts it with denial without thought, reflection, or consideration; rather, at the very time of its coming he denies it.

Then He threatens them with a threat containing belittlement of them, in the manner of a rebuke. The word "for the disbelievers" is where the apparent noun is placed in the position of the pronoun, i.e., "an abode for them." In this there is an alert to the cause of their lying and denial, which is disbelief (kufr).

﴿And the one who brings the truth﴾ is parallel to His saying: "Who then is more unjust."

﴿And confirms it﴾ is opposite to His saying: ﴿and denies the truth﴾. ("Alladhi") is a generic term, as if He said: "And the group who brought the truth." This is indicated by ﴿those are the righteous﴾, so He used the plural. Just as the intended meaning of "who then is more unjust" is a plural, which is why He said "an abode for the disbelievers."

In the recitation of Abdullah (Ibn Mas'ud): "And those who brought the truth and confirmed it" (wa-lladhi ja'u bi-l-sidq wa-saddaqu bihi). It was said: He intended "alladhina" (those who), and the nun was dropped. This is not correct, since if "alladhina" were intended with the form "alladhi" and the nun dropped, the pronoun would have been plural, as in His saying:

*"And indeed, those whose blood was shed at Falh..."*

Do you not see that when the nun is dropped in the dual, the pronoun becomes dual? As in His saying:

*"Sons of Kulayb, indeed my two uncles, who killed the kings and freed the shackles."*

It was said: "The one who brought the truth and confirmed it" is the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ).

It was said: "The one who brought the truth" is Jibril (Gabriel), and "the one who confirmed it" is Muhammad (ﷺ).

Ali, Abu al-'Aliya, al-Kalbi, and a group said: "The one who brought the truth" is the Messenger, and "the one who confirmed it" is Abu Bakr.

Abu al-Aswad, Mujahid, and a group said: "The one who confirmed it" is Ali ibn Abi Talib.

Al-Zamakhshari said: "And the one who brought the truth and confirmed it" is the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), who brought the truth and believed in it, and by it he intended himself and those who followed him, just as by Musa he intended himself and his people in His saying: ﴿And indeed We gave Musa the Book that they might be guided﴾ [Al-Mu'minun: 49]. For this reason He said: ﴿those are the righteous﴾, except that this is in the attribute and that is in the noun.

It is also permissible that the intended meaning is: the group and the company who brought the truth and confirmed it, namely the Messenger who brought the truth, and his companions who confirmed it. End of quote.

His statement "by it he intended himself and those who followed him, just as by Musa he intended himself and his people" uses the detached pronoun in a place where it should be attached. The correct form would be: "and intended him by it and those who followed him, just as he intended him with Musa and his people," meaning: "perhaps his people would be guided," since Musa (peace be upon him) is himself guided. Thus what is hoped for is the guidance of his people, not his own guidance, since only what is absent, not what is present, is hoped for.

His statement "and it is permissible etc." contains a distribution of the relative clause (tawzi' al-silah), where "the group" is the relative antecedent; it is like his saying: "The group came, which was honored and honored others." The more apparent view is that there is no distribution; rather, what is conjoined to the relative clause is a relative clause for the one who has the first relative clause.

Al-Jumhur (the majority) recited "wa-saddaqa" with shaddah (emphatic), while Abu Salih, 'Ikrima ibn Sulayman, and Muhammad ibn Juhaza recited it without shaddah. Abu Salih said: "and acted upon it."

It was said: "he deserved by it the name of truthfulness." Ibn 'Atiyya said: "According to this, all the verbs are ascribed to Muhammad (ﷺ), and his community is implicitly included in the speech, and this is what makes ﴿those are the righteous﴾ fitting." End of quote.

Al-Zamakhshari said: that is, "he confirmed the people by it and did not lie to them about it," meaning: he conveyed it to them as it was revealed to him, without distortion. It was also said: its meaning is "he became truthful by it," i.e., by means of it, because the Qur'an is a miracle, and a miracle is a confirmation from the Wise One who does not do what is ugly toward the one through whose hands it is performed, and it is not permissible that one should be confirmed except a truthful one, so he becomes truthful by the miracle.

It has been recited: ﴿wa-saddaqa bihi﴾ (with the verb in the passive form, shaddah). End of quote. He means: in the passive voice with shaddah. The author of al-Lawami' said: "He came with truth from Allah, and he confirmed it by His word," i.e., in His word or in His coming, so the two qualities of truth were combined for him: his truthfulness from Allah, and his truthfulness in himself, and this is an intensification in praise. End of quote.

(p-427)

Commentary of Abu Hayyan (al-Bahr al-Muhit) on surah 39, verse 32–40 (part 2 of 2):

﴿They shall have whatever they wish﴾: general in respect of everything their souls desire and their wills are directed toward. And ﴿so that﴾ (li-yukaffira): it is connected either to "the good-doers," meaning: those who did good, so that [Allah] may expiate; or to an omitted element, meaning: He facilitated that for them so that He may expiate, because expiation only occurs after facilitation toward good. And ﴿the worst of what they did﴾ refers to the disbelief of the people of ignorance (jahiliyyah) and the sins of the people of Islam. (p-429) Expiation indicates the removal of punishment from them in the most complete manner, and recompense with "the best" indicates the attainment of reward in the most complete manner. It has been said: that occurs when they affirm the prophets in what they brought. Muqatil said: He recompenses them with the good deeds among their actions and does not recompense them with the bad ones. This is the view of the Murji'ah, who say: no sin harms alongside faith. They argued with this verse. The apparent noun stands in place of the pronoun in "the good-doers," meaning: that is their recompense, so by the apparent noun He draws attention to the cause that necessitates the attainment of reward. The apparent reading is that "worst" (asw'a) is an elative (af'al al-tafdil), and with it the majority (al-Jumhur) read: "and when He expiates the worst of their deeds," so expiating what is lesser than it is more fitting. It has been said: af'al is not for comparison, and it is like your saying: "al-Ashajj is the most just of the Banu Marwan," meaning: just. Likewise here, meaning: "the evil of those who did [evil]."
This interpretation is supported by the reading of Ibn Miqsam and Hamid ibn Yahya, from Ibn Kathir: "asw'a" here; and in (Ha Mim al-Sajdah) with an alif between the waw and the hamzah, the plural of "su'" (evil), in which there is no elative. The apparent reading is that ﴿the best﴾ is an elative. It has been said: ﴿so that He may look at the best of their acts, and the remainder is recompensed by analogy to it, even if it falls short of that through shortcoming.﴾ It has been said: ﴿the best reward of their deeds.﴾ It has been said: ﴿the best of their deed, which is Paradise,﴾ and this is repelled by ﴿the best of what﴾.

Al-Zamakhshari said: As for the elative, it indicates that the thing which befalls them of minor sins and slips that are expiated is, in their view, the worst, because of their great regard for disobedience, while the good they do is, with Allah, the best, because of the sincerity of their intention in it. Therefore He mentioned their evil with "the worst" and their good with "the best." End.

This is according to the view of the Mu'tazilah, and it would make "asw'a" an elative according to their belief and "ahsan" an elative according to what is with Allah; and that is a distribution (tawzi') in the elative, which is contrary to the apparent meaning.

The Quraysh said: "If Muhammad does not desist from disparaging our gods and disparaging us, we will set them upon him so that they afflict him with madness and strike him with evil." So Allah revealed: ﴿Is not Allah sufficient for His servant?﴾ meaning: sufficient against the evil of whoever intends him with harm. The hamzah entering upon the negation is for affirmation, meaning: He is sufficient for His servant. In attributing him to Himself there is a great honour for His Prophet. The majority read ﴿ʿabdahu﴾ ("His servant"), and this is the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ). Abu Ja'far, Mujahid, Ibn Wathhab, Talhah, al-A'mash, Hamzah and al-Kisa'i read ﴿ʿibadahu﴾ ("His servants") in the plural, meaning: the prophets and the obedient believers.

﴿And they frighten you with those other than Him﴾: namely the idols. When [the Prophet] sent Khalid to break al-'Uzza, its custodian said to him: "I fear for you from it, for it has a power before which nothing stands." Khalid took the axe, struck its face with it and shattered it, then departed. In His saying ﴿they frighten you﴾ there is mockery of them, because they frightened him with what cannot benefit or harm. A parallel to this frightening is the saying of the people of Hud to him: ﴿We only say that some of our gods have struck you with evil﴾ [Hud: 54]. It was also read: ﴿bi-kafin ʿabdahu﴾ ("with a sufficient one of His servant") in the genitive construction, and ﴿yukafi ʿibadahu﴾ as the present tense of kafa, with ﴿ʿibadahu﴾ in the accusative. It is possible that it is a mufa'alah from sufficiency (al-kifayah), like your saying "yujazi" for "yajzi," and it is more emphatic than kafa, for being built upon the form of intensification; and this is the apparent reading because of the frequent recurrence of this meaning in the Qur'an, as in His saying: ﴿So Allah will suffice you against them﴾ [al-Baqarah: 137]. It is also possible that it is hamzated from al-mukafa'ah, which is recompense, meaning: He will recompense them their reward.

Since the Exalted is sufficient for His servant, frightening with other than Him is vain and false.

Since the verse contains both the guided and the misguided, He informed that all of that is done by Him. Then He said: ﴿Is not Allah Mighty﴾, meaning: victorious, unassailable, ﴿Lord of retribution﴾. In this there is a threat to the Quraysh and a promise to the believers.

Since they acknowledged the Creator, who is Allah, He informed them that He, the Exalted, is the One who disposes of His Prophet as He wills. For those idols which they claim to be gods besides Him cannot remove harm nor withhold mercy, meaning: health and abundance in provision and the like.

"Have you considered?" here is used in its original form; it took its first object, which is ﴿what you call upon﴾. The second object came as an interrogative clause, and in it is the pronoun referring back to "what," namely the word ﴿hunna﴾, and it was made feminine to belittle them, render them powerless and diminish them. Among them were those named with female names, such as al-'Uzza, Manat and al-Lat.

He attributed the will of Allah regarding harm to Himself and mercy to Himself, because they frightened him with their harm, so He secured from them the admission that the Creator of the world is Allah.

Then He asked them about their idols: do they remove evil (p-430) and bring about good? The majority read ﴿kashifatu wa-mumsikatu﴾ with the genitive construction; Shaybah, al-A'raj, Amr ibn 'Ubayd and 'Isa read it with variation from him; Abu 'Amr and Abu Bakr read them with tanwin and the accusative for what follows them.

Since it was established that He, the Exalted, is sufficient for him, and that their idols neither harm nor benefit, He commanded him to know that He, the Exalted, is his sufficiency, meaning: his sufficient one. The answer to this question is omitted, and the estimate is: "Surely they will say: you have no power over any of that." Muqatil said: He asked them and they were silent.

﴿Say: O my people, act﴾: the discussion of its parallel has already preceded.

﴿Who then is more unjust than one who lies about Allah and denies the truth when it comes to him? Is there not in Hell an abode for the disbelievers?﴾ ﴿And the one who brings the truth and confirms it: those are the righteous.﴾ ﴿For them is whatever they wish with their Lord. That is the reward of the good-doers.﴾ ﴿That Allah may expiate from them the worst of what they did and reward them with the best of what they used to do.﴾ ﴿Is Allah not sufficient for His servant? Yet they frighten you with those other than Him. And whomever Allah leaves astray, for him there is no guide.﴾ ﴿And whomever Allah guides, for him there is no misleader. Is Allah not Mighty, Lord of Retribution?﴾ ﴿And if you asked them, "Who created the heavens and the earth?" they would surely say, "Allah." Say, "Have you considered what you invoke besides Allah? If Allah intends harm for me, can they remove His harm? Or if He intends mercy for me, can they withhold His mercy?" Say, "Allah is sufficient for me; upon Him rely those who rely."﴾ ﴿Say, "O my people, act according to your position; indeed I am acting. So you will soon know.﴾ ﴿Upon whom will come a punishment that disgraces him, and upon whom will descend a lasting punishment."﴾ ﴿Indeed, We have sent down to you the Book for mankind with the truth. So whoever is guided, it is for his own self; and whoever goes astray, he strays only to its detriment. And you are not a guardian over them.﴾ [Az-Zumar: 41] ﴿Allah takes the souls at the time of their death, and those that have not died during their sleep. Then He keeps those for which He has decreed death and releases the others until a specified term. Indeed, in that are signs for a people who reflect.﴾ [Az-Zumar: 42] ﴿Or have they taken intercessors besides Allah? Say, "Even though they possess nothing and do not understand?"﴾ [Az-Zumar: 43] (p-426) ﴿Say, "To Allah belongs all intercession. To Him belongs the dominion of the heavens and the earth. The word "for the disbelievers" is where the apparent noun is placed in the position of the pronoun, i.e., "an abode for them." In this there is an alert to the cause of their lying and denial, which is disbelief (kufr).

﴿And the one who brings the truth﴾ is parallel to His saying: "Who then is more unjust."

﴿And confirms it﴾ is opposite to His saying: ﴿and denies the truth﴾. ("Alladhi") is a generic term, as if He said: "And the group who brought the truth." This is indicated by ﴿those are the righteous﴾, so He used the plural. Just as the intended meaning of "who then is more unjust" is a plural, which is why He said "an abode for the disbelievers."

In the recitation of Abdullah (Ibn Mas'ud): "And those who brought the truth and confirmed it" (wa-lladhi ja'u bi-l-sidq wa-saddaqu bihi). It was said: He intended "alladhina" (those who), and the nun was dropped. This is not correct, since if "alladhina" were intended with the form "alladhi" and the nun dropped, the pronoun would have been plural, as in His saying:

*"And indeed, those whose blood was shed at Falh..."*

Do you not see that when the nun is dropped in the dual, the pronoun becomes dual? As in His saying:

*"Sons of Kulayb, indeed my two uncles, who killed the kings and freed the shackles."*

It was said: "The one who brought the truth and confirmed it" is the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ).

It was said: "The one who brought the truth" is Jibril (Gabriel), and "the one who confirmed it" is Muhammad (ﷺ).

Ali, Abu al-'Aliya, al-Kalbi, and a group said: "The one who brought the truth" is the Messenger, and "the one who confirmed it" is Abu Bakr.

Abu al-Aswad, Mujahid, and a group said: "The one who confirmed it" is Ali ibn Abi Talib.

Al-Zamakhshari said: "And the one who brought the truth and confirmed it" is the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), who brought the truth and believed in it, and by it he intended himself and those who followed him, just as by Musa he intended himself and his people in His saying: ﴿And indeed We gave Musa the Book that they might be guided﴾ [Al-Mu'minun: 49]. For this reason He said: ﴿those are the righteous﴾, except that this is in the attribute and that is in the noun.

It is also permissible that the intended meaning is: the group and the company who brought the truth and confirmed it, namely the Messenger who brought the truth, and his companions who confirmed it. End of quote.

His statement "by it he intended himself and those who followed him, just as by Musa he intended himself and his people" uses the detached pronoun in a place where it should be attached. The correct form would be: "and intended him by it and those who followed him, just as he intended him with Musa and his people," meaning: "perhaps his people would be guided," since Musa (peace be upon him) is himself guided. Thus what is hoped for is the guidance of his people, not his own guidance, since only what is absent, not what is present, is hoped for.

His statement "and it is permissible etc." contains a distribution of the relative clause (tawzi' al-silah), where "the group" is the relative antecedent; it is like his saying: "The group came, which was honored and honored others." The more apparent view is that there is no distribution; rather, what is conjoined to the relative clause is a relative clause for the one who has the first relative clause.

Al-Jumhur (the majority) recited "wa-saddaqa" with shaddah (emphatic), while Abu Salih, 'Ikrima ibn Sulayman, and Muhammad ibn Juhaza recited it without shaddah. Abu Salih said: "and acted upon it."

It was said: "he deserved by it the name of truthfulness." Ibn 'Atiyya said: "According to this, all the verbs are ascribed to Muhammad (ﷺ), and his community is implicitly included in the speech, and this is what makes ﴿those are the righteous﴾ fitting." End of quote.

Al-Zamakhshari said: that is, "he confirmed the people by it and did not lie to them about it," meaning: he conveyed it to them as it was revealed to him, without distortion. It was also said: its meaning is "he became truthful by it," i.e., by means of it, because the Qur'an is a miracle, and a miracle is a confirmation from the Wise One who does not do what is ugly toward the one through whose hands it is performed, and it is not permissible that one should be confirmed except a truthful one, so he becomes truthful by the miracle.

It has been recited: ﴿wa-saddaqa bihi﴾ (with the verb in the passive form, shaddah). End of quote. He means: in the passive voice with shaddah. The author of al-Lawami' said: "He came with truth from Allah, and he confirmed it by His word," i.e., in His word or in His coming, so the two qualities of truth were combined for him: his truthfulness from Allah, and his truthfulness in himself, and this is an intensification in praise. End of quote.

(p-427)

Commentary of Abu Hayyan (al-Bahr al-Muhit) on surah 39, verse 32–40 (part 2 of 2):

﴿They shall have whatever they wish﴾: general in respect of everything their souls desire and their wills are directed toward. And ﴿so that﴾ (li-yukaffira): it is connected either to "the good-doers," meaning: those who did good, so that [Allah] may expiate; or to an omitted element, meaning: He facilitated that for them so that He may expiate, because expiation only occurs after facilitation toward good. And ﴿the worst of what they did﴾ refers to the disbelief of the people of ignorance (jahiliyyah) and the sins of the people of Islam. (p-429) Expiation indicates the removal of punishment from them in the most complete manner, and recompense with "the best" indicates the attainment of reward in the most complete manner. It has been said: that occurs when they affirm the prophets in what they brought. Muqatil said: He recompenses them with the good deeds among their actions and does not recompense them with the bad ones. This is the view of the Murji'ah, who say: no sin harms alongside faith. They argued with this verse. The apparent noun stands in place of the pronoun in "the good-doers," meaning: that is their recompense, so by the apparent noun He draws attention to the cause that necessitates the attainment of reward. The apparent reading is that "worst" (asw'a) is an elative (af'al al-tafdil), and with it the majority (al-Jumhur) read: "and when He expiates the worst of their deeds," so expiating what is lesser than it is more fitting. It has been said: af'al is not for comparison, and it is like your saying: "al-Ashajj is the most just of the Banu Marwan," meaning: just. Likewise here, meaning: "the evil of those who did [evil]."
This interpretation is supported by the reading of Ibn Miqsam and Hamid ibn Yahya, from Ibn Kathir: "asw'a" here; and in (Ha Mim al-Sajdah) with an alif between the waw and the hamzah, the plural of "su'" (evil), in which there is no elative. The apparent reading is that ﴿the best﴾ is an elative. It has been said: ﴿so that He may look at the best of their acts, and the remainder is recompensed by analogy to it, even if it falls short of that through shortcoming.﴾ It has been said: ﴿the best reward of their deeds.﴾ It has been said: ﴿the best of their deed, which is Paradise,﴾ and this is repelled by ﴿the best of what﴾.

Al-Zamakhshari said: As for the elative, it indicates that the thing which befalls them of minor sins and slips that are expiated is, in their view, the worst, because of their great regard for disobedience, while the good they do is, with Allah, the best, because of the sincerity of their intention in it. Therefore He mentioned their evil with "the worst" and their good with "the best." End.

This is according to the view of the Mu'tazilah, and it would make "asw'a" an elative according to their belief and "ahsan" an elative according to what is with Allah; and that is a distribution (tawzi') in the elative, which is contrary to the apparent meaning.

The Quraysh said: "If Muhammad does not desist from disparaging our gods and disparaging us, we will set them upon him so that they afflict him with madness and strike him with evil." So Allah revealed: ﴿Is not Allah sufficient for His servant?﴾ meaning: sufficient against the evil of whoever intends him with harm. The hamzah entering upon the negation is for affirmation, meaning: He is sufficient for His servant. In attributing him to Himself there is a great honour for His Prophet. The majority read ﴿ʿabdahu﴾ ("His servant"), and this is the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ). Abu Ja'far, Mujahid, Ibn Wathhab, Talhah, al-A'mash, Hamzah and al-Kisa'i read ﴿ʿibadahu﴾ ("His servants") in the plural, meaning: the prophets and the obedient believers.

﴿And they frighten you with those other than Him﴾: namely the idols. When [the Prophet] sent Khalid to break al-'Uzza, its custodian said to him: "I fear for you from it, for it has a power before which nothing stands." Khalid took the axe, struck its face with it and shattered it, then departed. In His saying ﴿they frighten you﴾ there is mockery of them, because they frightened him with what cannot benefit or harm. A parallel to this frightening is the saying of the people of Hud to him: ﴿We only say that some of our gods have struck you with evil﴾ [Hud: 54]. It was also read: ﴿bi-kafin ʿabdahu﴾ ("with a sufficient one of His servant") in the genitive construction, and ﴿yukafi ʿibadahu﴾ as the present tense of kafa, with ﴿ʿibadahu﴾ in the accusative. It is possible that it is a mufa'alah from sufficiency (al-kifayah), like your saying "yujazi" for "yajzi," and it is more emphatic than kafa, for being built upon the form of intensification; and this is the apparent reading because of the frequent recurrence of this meaning in the Qur'an, as in His saying: ﴿So Allah will suffice you against them﴾ [al-Baqarah: 137]. It is also possible that it is hamzated from al-mukafa'ah, which is recompense, meaning: He will recompense them their reward.

Since the Exalted is sufficient for His servant, frightening with other than Him is vain and false.

Since the verse contains both the guided and the misguided, He informed that all of that is done by Him. Then He said: ﴿Is not Allah Mighty﴾, meaning: victorious, unassailable, ﴿Lord of retribution﴾. In this there is a threat to the Quraysh and a promise to the believers.

Since they acknowledged the Creator, who is Allah, He informed them that He, the Exalted, is the One who disposes of His Prophet as He wills. For those idols which they claim to be gods besides Him cannot remove harm nor withhold mercy, meaning: health and abundance in provision and the like.

"Have you considered?" here is used in its original form; it took its first object, which is ﴿what you call upon﴾. The second object came as an interrogative clause, and in it is the pronoun referring back to "what," namely the word ﴿hunna﴾, and it was made feminine to belittle them, render them powerless and diminish them. Among them were those named with female names, such as al-'Uzza, Manat and al-Lat.

He attributed the will of Allah regarding harm to Himself and mercy to Himself, because they frightened him with their harm, so He secured from them the admission that the Creator of the world is Allah.

Then He asked them about their idols: do they remove evil (p-430) and bring about good? The majority read ﴿kashifatu wa-mumsikatu﴾ with the genitive construction; Shaybah, al-A'raj, Amr ibn 'Ubayd and 'Isa read it with variation from him; Abu 'Amr and Abu Bakr read them with tanwin and the accusative for what follows them.

Since it was established that He, the Exalted, is sufficient for him, and that their idols neither harm nor benefit, He commanded him to know that He, the Exalted, is his sufficiency, meaning: his sufficient one. The answer to this question is omitted, and the estimate is: "Surely they will say: you have no power over any of that." Muqatil said: He asked them and they were silent.

﴿Say: O my people, act﴾: the discussion of its parallel has already preceded.

﴿Who then is more unjust than one who lies about Allah and denies the truth when it comes to him? Is there not in Hell an abode for the disbelievers?﴾ ﴿And the one who brings the truth and confirms it: those are the righteous.﴾ ﴿For them is whatever they wish with their Lord. That is the reward of the good-doers.﴾ ﴿That Allah may expiate from them the worst of what they did and reward them with the best of what they used to do.﴾ ﴿Is Allah not sufficient for His servant? Yet they frighten you with those other than Him. And whomever Allah leaves astray, for him there is no guide.﴾ ﴿And whomever Allah guides, for him there is no misleader. Is Allah not Mighty, Lord of Retribution?﴾ ﴿And if you asked them, "Who created the heavens and the earth?" they would surely say, "Allah." Say, "Have you considered what you invoke besides Allah? If Allah intends harm for me, can they remove His harm? Or if He intends mercy for me, can they withhold His mercy?" Say, "Allah is sufficient for me; upon Him rely those who rely."﴾ ﴿Say, "O my people, act according to your position; indeed I am acting. So you will soon know.﴾ ﴿Upon whom will come a punishment that disgraces him, and upon whom will descend a lasting punishment."﴾ ﴿Indeed, We have sent down to you the Book for mankind with the truth. So whoever is guided, it is for his own self; and whoever goes astray, he strays only to its detriment. And you are not a guardian over them.﴾ [Az-Zumar: 41] ﴿Allah takes the souls at the time of their death, and those that have not died during their sleep. Then He keeps those for which He has decreed death and releases the others until a specified term. Indeed, in that are signs for a people who reflect.﴾ [Az-Zumar: 42] ﴿Or have they taken intercessors besides Allah? Say, "Even though they possess nothing and do not understand?"﴾ [Az-Zumar: 43] (p-426) ﴿Say, "To Allah belongs all intercession. To Him belongs the dominion of the heavens and the earth. Then to Him you will be returned."﴾ [Az-Zumar: 44] ﴿And when Allah alone is mentioned, the hearts of those who do not believe in the Hereafter shrink; but when those other than Him are mentioned, behold, they rejoice.﴾ [Az-Zumar: 45] ﴿Say, "O Allah, Creator of the heavens and the earth, Knower of the unseen and the witnessed, You will judge between Your servants concerning that over which they used to differ."﴾ [Az-Zumar: 46] ﴿And if those who wronged had all that is in the earth and the like of it with it, they would surely ransom themselves with it from the evil of the punishment on the Day of Resurrection. And there will appear to them from Allah what they had not expected.﴾ [Az-Zumar: 47] ﴿And there will appear to them the evils of what they earned, and they will be surrounded by that which they used to mock.﴾ [Az-Zumar: 48] ﴿So when harm touches man, he calls upon Us; then when We bestow upon him a favor from Us, he says, "I was given it only because of knowledge." Rather, it is a trial, but most of them do not know.﴾ [Az-Zumar: 49] ﴿Those before them had said it, but what they used to earn did not avail them.﴾ [Az-Zumar: 50] ﴿So the evils of what they earned struck them. And those who wronged among these will be struck by the evils of what they earned, and they cannot escape.﴾ [Az-Zumar: 51] ﴿Do they not know that Allah extends provision to whom He wills and restricts it? Indeed, in that are signs for a people who believe.﴾ [Az-Zumar: 52] ﴿Say, "O My servants who have transgressed against themselves, do not despair of the mercy of Allah. Indeed, Allah forgives all sins. Indeed, He is the Forgiving, the Merciful."﴾ [Az-Zumar: 53] ﴿And turn in repentance to your Lord and submit to Him before the punishment comes upon you, after which you will not be helped.﴾ [Az-Zumar: 54] ﴿And follow the best of what was revealed to you from your Lord before the punishment comes upon you suddenly while you do not perceive.﴾ [Az-Zumar: 55] ﴿Lest a soul should say, "Oh, my regret over what I neglected in regard to Allah, and indeed I was among the mockers."﴾ [Az-Zumar: 56] ﴿Or lest it say, "If only Allah had guided me, I would have been among the righteous."﴾ [Az-Zumar: 57] ﴿Or lest it say when it sees the punishment, "If only I had another return, I would be among the good-doers."﴾ [Az-Zumar: 58] ﴿[It will be said], "Yes, indeed My verses came to you, but you denied them, grew arrogant, and were among the disbelievers."﴾ [Az-Zumar: 59] ﴿And on the Day of Resurrection you will see those who lied about Allah with their faces blackened. Is there not in Hell an abode for the arrogant?﴾ [Az-Zumar: 60] ﴿And Allah will save those who were righteous by their achievement; no harm will touch them, nor will they grieve.﴾ [Az-Zumar: 61] ﴿Allah is the Creator of all things, and He is the Guardian over all things.﴾ [Az-Zumar: 62] ﴿To Him belong the keys of the heavens and the earth. And those who disbelieved in the signs of Allah, those are the losers.﴾ [Az-Zumar: 63] ﴿Say, "Do you command me to worship other than Allah, O ignorant ones?"﴾ [Az-Zumar: 64] ﴿And it has been revealed to you and to those before you: "If you associate partners with Allah, your deeds will surely be lost, and you will surely be among the losers."﴾ [Az-Zumar: 65] ﴿Rather, worship Allah alone and be among the grateful.﴾ [Az-Zumar: 66] ﴿They did not measure Allah with His true measure. And the earth entirely in His grip on the Day of Resurrection, and the heavens folded in His right hand. Glorified is He and exalted above what they associate with Him.﴾ [Az-Zumar: 67] ﴿And the Trumpet will be blown, and whoever is in the heavens and whoever is on the earth will fall unconscious, except whom Allah wills. Then it will be blown again, and immediately they will be standing, looking on.﴾ [Az-Zumar: 68] ﴿And the earth will shine with the light of its Lord, the Record will be placed, the prophets and the witnesses will be brought, and judgment will be given between them with truth, and they will not be wronged.﴾ [Az-Zumar: 69] ﴿And every soul will be paid in full for what it did, and He is most knowing of what they do.﴾ [Az-Zumar: 70] ﴿And those who disbelieved will be driven to Hell in groups, until when they reach it, its gates will be opened, and its keepers will say to them, "Did there not come to you messengers from among you reciting to you the verses of your Lord and warning you of the meeting of this your Day?" They will say, "Yes, but the word of punishment has come due upon the disbelievers."﴾ [Az-Zumar: 71] ﴿It will be said, "Enter the gates of Hell, to abide therein. How wretched is the abode of the arrogant."﴾ [Az-Zumar: 72] ﴿And those who feared their Lord will be driven to Paradise in groups, until when they reach it, and its gates are opened, its keepers will say to them, "Peace be upon you; you are good, so enter it to abide therein."﴾ [Az-Zumar: 73] ﴿And they will say, "Praise be to Allah, who has fulfilled His promise to us and has caused us to inherit the earth, to dwell in Paradise wherever we will. How excellent is the reward of the workers."﴾ [Az-Zumar: 74] ﴿And you will see the angels surrounding the Throne, glorifying their Lord with His praise. And judgment will be given between them with truth, and it will be said, "Praise be to Allah, Lord of the worlds."﴾ [Az-Zumar: 75].

It has been said: ﴿so that He may look at the best of their acts, and the remainder is recompensed by analogy to it, even if it falls short of that through shortcoming.﴾ It has been said: ﴿the best reward of their deeds.﴾ It has been said: ﴿the best of their deed, which is Paradise,﴾ and this is repelled by ﴿the best of what﴾.

Al-Zamakhshari said: As for the elative, it indicates that the thing which befalls them of minor sins and slips that are expiated is, in their view, the worst, because of their great regard for disobedience, while the good they do is, with Allah, the best, because of the sincerity of their intention in it. Therefore He mentioned their evil with "the worst" and their good with "the best." End.

This is according to the view of the Mu'tazilah, and it would make "asw'a" an elative according to their belief and "ahsan" an elative according to what is with Allah; and that is a distribution (tawzi') in the elative, which is contrary to the apparent meaning.

The Quraysh said: "If Muhammad does not desist from disparaging our gods and disparaging us, we will set them upon him so that they afflict him with madness and strike him with evil." So Allah revealed: ﴿Is not Allah sufficient for His servant?﴾ meaning: sufficient against the evil of whoever intends him with harm. The hamzah entering upon the negation is for affirmation, meaning: He is sufficient for His servant. In attributing him to Himself there is a great honour for His Prophet. The majority read ﴿ʿabdahu﴾ ("His servant"), and this is the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ). Abu Ja'far, Mujahid, Ibn Wathhab, Talhah, al-A'mash, Hamzah and al-Kisa'i read ﴿ʿibadahu﴾ ("His servants") in the plural, meaning: the prophets and the obedient believers.

﴿And they frighten you with those other than Him﴾: namely the idols. When [the Prophet] sent Khalid to break al-'Uzza, its custodian said to him: "I fear for you from it, for it has a power before which nothing stands." Khalid took the axe, struck its face with it and shattered it, then departed. In His saying ﴿they frighten you﴾ there is mockery of them, because they frightened him with what cannot benefit or harm. A parallel to this frightening is the saying of the people of Hud to him: ﴿We only say that some of our gods have struck you with evil﴾ [Hud: 54]. It was also read: ﴿bi-kafin ʿabdahu﴾ ("with a sufficient one of His servant") in the genitive construction, and ﴿yukafi ʿibadahu﴾ as the present tense of kafa, with ﴿ʿibadahu﴾ in the accusative. It is possible that it is a mufa'alah from sufficiency (al-kifayah), like your saying "yujazi" for "yajzi," and it is more emphatic than kafa, for being built upon the form of intensification; and this is the apparent reading because of the frequent recurrence of this meaning in the Qur'an, as in His saying: ﴿So Allah will suffice you against them﴾ [al-Baqarah: 137]. It is also possible that it is hamzated from al-mukafa'ah, which is recompense, meaning: He will recompense them their reward.

Since the Exalted is sufficient for His servant, frightening with other than Him is vain and false.

Since the verse contains both the guided and the misguided, He informed that all of that is done by Him. Then He said: ﴿Is not Allah Mighty﴾, meaning: victorious, unassailable, ﴿Lord of retribution﴾. In this there is a threat to the Quraysh and a promise to the believers.

Since they acknowledged the Creator, who is Allah, He informed them that He, the Exalted, is the One who disposes of His Prophet as He wills. For those idols which they claim to be gods besides Him cannot remove harm nor withhold mercy, meaning: health and abundance in provision and the like.

"Have you considered?" here is used in its original form; it took its first object, which is ﴿what you call upon﴾. The second object came as an interrogative clause, and in it is the pronoun referring back to "what," namely the word ﴿hunna﴾, and it was made feminine to belittle them, render them powerless and diminish them. Among them were those named with female names, such as al-'Uzza, Manat and al-Lat.

He attributed the will of Allah regarding harm to Himself and mercy to Himself, because they frightened him with their harm, so He secured from them the admission that the Creator of the world is Allah.

Then He asked them about their idols: do they remove evil (p-430) and bring about good? The majority read ﴿kashifatu wa-mumsikatu﴾ with the genitive construction; Shaybah, al-A'raj, Amr ibn 'Ubayd and 'Isa read it with variation from him; Abu 'Amr and Abu Bakr read them with tanwin and the accusative for what follows them.

Since it was established that He, the Exalted, is sufficient for him, and that their idols neither harm nor benefit, He commanded him to know that He, the Exalted, is his sufficiency, meaning: his sufficient one. The answer to this question is omitted, and the estimate is: "Surely they will say: you have no power over any of that." Muqatil said: He asked them and they were silent.

﴿Say: O my people, act﴾: the discussion of its parallel has already preceded.

﴿Who then is more unjust than one who lies about Allah and denies the truth when it comes to him? Is there not in Hell an abode for the disbelievers?﴾ ﴿And the one who brings the truth and confirms it: those are the righteous.﴾ ﴿For them is whatever they wish with their Lord. That is the reward of the good-doers.﴾ ﴿That Allah may expiate from them the worst of what they did and reward them with the best of what they used to do.﴾ ﴿Is Allah not sufficient for His servant? Yet they frighten you with those other than Him. And whomever Allah leaves astray, for him there is no guide.﴾ ﴿And whomever Allah guides, for him there is no misleader. Is Allah not Mighty, Lord of Retribution?﴾ ﴿And if you asked them, "Who created the heavens and the earth?" they would surely say, "Allah." Say, "Have you considered what you invoke besides Allah? If Allah intends harm for me, can they remove His harm? Or if He intends mercy for me, can they withhold His mercy?" Say, "Allah is sufficient for me; upon Him rely those who rely."﴾ ﴿Say, "O my people, act according to your position; indeed I am acting. So you will soon know.﴾ ﴿Upon whom will come a punishment that disgraces him, and upon whom will descend a lasting punishment."﴾ ﴿Indeed, We have sent down to you the Book for mankind with the truth. So whoever is guided, it is for his own self; and whoever goes astray, he strays only to its detriment. And you are not a guardian over them.﴾ [Az-Zumar: 41] ﴿Allah takes the souls at the time of their death, and those that have not died during their sleep. Then He keeps those for which He has decreed death and releases the others until a specified term. Indeed, in that are signs for a people who reflect.﴾ [Az-Zumar: 42] ﴿Or have they taken intercessors besides Allah? Say, "Even though they possess nothing and do not understand?"﴾ [Az-Zumar: 43] (p-426) ﴿Say, "To Allah belongs all intercession. To Him belongs the dominion of the heavens and the earth. Then to Him you will be returned."﴾ [Az-Zumar: 44] ﴿And when Allah alone is mentioned, the hearts of those who do not believe in the Hereafter shrink; but when those other than Him are mentioned, behold, they rejoice.﴾ [Az-Zumar: 45] ﴿Say, "O Allah, Creator of the heavens and the earth, Knower of the unseen and the witnessed, You will judge between Your servants concerning that over which they used to differ."﴾ [Az-Zumar: 46] ﴿And if those who wronged had all that is in the earth and the like of it with it, they would surely ransom themselves with it from the evil of the punishment on the Day of Resurrection. And there will appear to them from Allah what they had not expected.﴾ [Az-Zumar: 47] ﴿And there will appear to them the evils of what they earned, and they will be surrounded by that which they used to mock.﴾ [Az-Zumar: 48] ﴿So when harm touches man, he calls upon Us; then when We bestow upon him a favor from Us, he says, "I was given it only because of knowledge." Rather, it is a trial, but most of them do not know.﴾ [Az-Zumar: 49] ﴿Those before them had said it, but what they used to earn did not avail them.﴾ [Az-Zumar: 50] ﴿So the evils of what they earned struck them. And those who wronged among these will be struck by the evils of what they earned, and they cannot escape.﴾ [Az-Zumar: 51] ﴿Do they not know that Allah extends provision to whom He wills and restricts it? Indeed, in that are signs for a people who believe.﴾ [Az-Zumar: 52] ﴿Say, "O My servants who have transgressed against themselves, do not despair of the mercy of Allah. Indeed, Allah forgives all sins. Indeed, He is the Forgiving, the Merciful."﴾ [Az-Zumar: 53] ﴿And turn in repentance to your Lord and submit to Him before the punishment comes upon you, after which you will not be helped.﴾ [Az-Zumar: 54] ﴿And follow the best of what was revealed to you from your Lord before the punishment comes upon you suddenly while you do not perceive.﴾ [Az-Zumar: 55] ﴿Lest a soul should say, "Oh, my regret over what I neglected in regard to Allah, and indeed I was among the mockers."﴾ [Az-Zumar: 56] ﴿Or lest it say, "If only Allah had guided me, I would have been among the righteous."﴾ [Az-Zumar: 57] ﴿Or lest it say when it sees the punishment, "If only I had another return, I would be among the good-doers."﴾ [Az-Zumar: 58] ﴿[It will be said], "Yes, indeed My verses came to you, but you denied them, grew arrogant, and were among the disbelievers."﴾ [Az-Zumar: 59] ﴿And on the Day of Resurrection you will see those who lied about Allah with their faces blackened. Is there not in Hell an abode for the arrogant?﴾ [Az-Zumar: 60] ﴿And Allah will save those who were righteous by their achievement; no harm will touch them, nor will they grieve.﴾ [Az-Zumar: 61] ﴿Allah is the Creator of all things, and He is the Guardian over all things.﴾ [Az-Zumar: 62] ﴿To Him belong the keys of the heavens and the earth. And those who disbelieved in the signs of Allah, those are the losers.﴾ [Az-Zumar: 63] ﴿Say, "Do you command me to worship other than Allah, O ignorant ones?"﴾ [Az-Zumar: 64] ﴿And it has been revealed to you and to those before you: "If you associate partners with Allah, your deeds will surely be lost, and you will surely be among the losers."﴾ [Az-Zumar: 65] ﴿Rather, worship Allah alone and be among the grateful.﴾ [Az-Zumar: 66] ﴿They did not measure Allah with His true measure. And the earth entirely in His grip on the Day of Resurrection, and the heavens folded in His right hand. Glorified is He and exalted above what they associate with Him.﴾ [Az-Zumar: 67] ﴿And the Trumpet will be blown, and whoever is in the heavens and whoever is on the earth will fall unconscious, except whom Allah wills. Then it will be blown again, and immediately they will be standing, looking on.﴾ [Az-Zumar: 68] ﴿And the earth will shine with the light of its Lord, the Record will be placed, the prophets and the witnesses will be brought, and judgment will be given between them with truth, and they will not be wronged.﴾ [Az-Zumar: 69] ﴿And every soul will be paid in full for what it did, and He is most knowing of what they do.﴾ [Az-Zumar: 70] ﴿And those who disbelieved will be driven to Hell in groups, until when they reach it, its gates will be opened, and its keepers will say to them, "Did there not come to you messengers from among you reciting to you the verses of your Lord and warning you of the meeting of this your Day?" They will say, "Yes, but the word of punishment has come due upon the disbelievers."﴾ [Az-Zumar: 71] ﴿It will be said, "Enter the gates of Hell, to abide therein. How wretched is the abode of the arrogant."﴾ [Az-Zumar: 72] ﴿And those who feared their Lord will be driven to Paradise in groups, until when they reach it, and its gates are opened, its keepers will say to them, "Peace be upon you; you are good, so enter it to abide therein."﴾ [Az-Zumar: 73] ﴿And they will say, "Praise be to Allah, who has fulfilled His promise to us and has caused us to inherit the earth, to dwell in Paradise wherever we will. How excellent is the reward of the workers."﴾ [Az-Zumar: 74] ﴿And you will see the angels surrounding the Throne, glorifying their Lord with His praise. And judgment will be given between them with truth, and it will be said, "Praise be to Allah, Lord of the worlds."﴾ [Az-Zumar: 75].

Ishma'azza (اشمأز): Abu Zayd said: "za'ira" (زعر). Others said: "taqabbaḍa karāhatan wa-nufūran" (it contracted from aversion and repulsion). The poet said:

*"When the trustworthy ones bite at it, it shrinks, and it turns away from him, rough and strong."*

Al-maqalid (المقاليد): the keys (al-mafatih). It was said: it has no singular from its own form, as stated by al-Tabrizi. It was also said: its singular is miqlid, and it was said: miqlad. It is said: iqlid and aqalid. The word originally is Persian.

Al-zumar (الزمر): the plural of zumra. Abu 'Ubayda and al-Akhfash said: separate groups, one following another. He said:

*"Until the groups gathered, one after another."*

It is said: tazammara (to form groups).

Al-hufuf (الحفوف): surrounding something (al-ihdaq bi-l-shay'). The poet said:

*"Surrounded by a narrow side, and followed by it, like a glass bottle not treated with kohl against sore eyes."*

This word is derived from al-hafaf, which is the side. From it is the saying of the poet:

*"For him are glances from the side of his throne, when he returns them there is punishment and bounty."*

﴿So who is more unjust than one who lies about Allah...﴾ up to ﴿...an abode for the disbelievers﴾ [quoted above]. ﴿...And the one who brings the truth and confirms it...﴾ [quoted above].

﴿Who then is more unjust than one who lies about Allah﴾: This is an explanation and clarification of those who have the dispute, and this indicates that the earlier dispute (ikhtisam) is between the believers and the disbelievers. The meaning: I find among the deniers no one more unjust than one who fabricates against Allah, attributing to Him a son, a consort, and a partner, and makes lawful and unlawful without the command of Allah.

﴿And denies the truth﴾: which is what the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) brought. ﴿When it comes to him﴾: i.e., at the time of its coming. He confronts it with denial without thought, reflection, or consideration; rather, at the very time of its coming he denies it.

Then He threatens them with a threat containing belittlement of them, in the manner of a rebuke. The word "for the disbelievers" is where the apparent noun is placed in the position of the pronoun, i.e., "an abode for them." In this there is an alert to the cause of their lying and denial, which is disbelief (kufr).

﴿And the one who brings the truth﴾ is parallel to His saying: "Who then is more unjust."

﴿And confirms it﴾ is opposite to His saying: ﴿and denies the truth﴾. ("Alladhi") is a generic term, as if He said: "And the group who brought the truth." This is indicated by ﴿those are the righteous﴾, so He used the plural. Just as the intended meaning of "who then is more unjust" is a plural, which is why He said "an abode for the disbelievers."

In the recitation of Abdullah (Ibn Mas'ud): "And those who brought the truth and confirmed it" (wa-lladhi ja'u bi-l-sidq wa-saddaqu bihi). It was said: He intended "alladhina" (those who), and the nun was dropped. This is not correct, since if "alladhina" were intended with the form "alladhi" and the nun dropped, the pronoun would have been plural, as in His saying:

*"And indeed, those whose blood was shed at Falh..."*

Do you not see that when the nun is dropped in the dual, the pronoun becomes dual? As in His saying:

*"Sons of Kulayb, indeed my two uncles, who killed the kings and freed the shackles."*

It was said: "The one who brought the truth and confirmed it" is the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ).

It was said: "The one who brought the truth" is Jibril (Gabriel), and "the one who confirmed it" is Muhammad (ﷺ).

Ali, Abu al-'Aliya, al-Kalbi, and a group said: "The one who brought the truth" is the Messenger, and "the one who confirmed it" is Abu Bakr.

Abu al-Aswad, Mujahid, and a group said: "The one who confirmed it" is Ali ibn Abi Talib.

Al-Zamakhshari said: "And the one who brought the truth and confirmed it" is the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), who brought the truth and believed in it, and by it he intended himself and those who followed him, just as by Musa he intended himself and his people in His saying: ﴿And indeed We gave Musa the Book that they might be guided﴾ [Al-Mu'minun: 49]. For this reason He said: ﴿those are the righteous﴾, except that this is in the attribute and that is in the noun.

It is also permissible that the intended meaning is: the group and the company who brought the truth and confirmed it, namely the Messenger who brought the truth, and his companions who confirmed it. End of quote.

His statement "by it he intended himself and those who followed him, just as by Musa he intended himself and his people" uses the detached pronoun in a place where it should be attached. The correct form would be: "and intended him by it and those who followed him, just as he intended him with Musa and his people," meaning: "perhaps his people would be guided," since Musa (peace be upon him) is himself guided. Thus what is hoped for is the guidance of his people, not his own guidance, since only what is absent, not what is present, is hoped for.

His statement "and it is permissible etc." contains a distribution of the relative clause (tawzi' al-silah), where "the group" is the relative antecedent; it is like his saying: "The group came, which was honored and honored others." The more apparent view is that there is no distribution; rather, what is conjoined to the relative clause is a relative clause for the one who has the first relative clause.

Al-Jumhur (the majority) recited "wa-saddaqa" with shaddah (emphatic), while Abu Salih, 'Ikrima ibn Sulayman, and Muhammad ibn Juhaza recited it without shaddah. Abu Salih said: "and acted upon it."

It was said: "he deserved by it the name of truthfulness." Ibn 'Atiyya said: "According to this, all the verbs are ascribed to Muhammad (ﷺ), and his community is implicitly included in the speech, and this is what makes ﴿those are the righteous﴾ fitting." End of quote.

Al-Zamakhshari said: that is, "he confirmed the people by it and did not lie to them about it," meaning: he conveyed it to them as it was revealed to him, without distortion. It was also said: its meaning is "he became truthful by it," i.e., by means of it, because the Qur'an is a miracle, and a miracle is a confirmation from the Wise One who does not do what is ugly toward the one through whose hands it is performed, and it is not permissible that one should be confirmed except a truthful one, so he becomes truthful by the miracle.

It has been recited: ﴿wa-saddaqa bihi﴾ (with the verb in the passive form, shaddah). End of quote. He means: in the passive voice with shaddah. The author of al-Lawami' said: "He came with truth from Allah, and he confirmed it by His word," i.e., in His word or in His coming, so the two qualities of truth were combined for him: his truthfulness from Allah, and his truthfulness in himself, and this is an intensification in praise. End of quote.

(p-427)
